prompt: Name one of the seven colours traditionally identified in a rainbow.
label: Easy Opener
valueLogic: Five of the seven are named by almost anyone, so they sit at 3-6. Violet is often said as purple, hence 10. Indigo is the one people genuinely forget and the only real tail, at 14.
note: Purple is kept as an alias for violet: in everyday English they're the same answer, and busting on it would read as a bug.

answers.name: Red
answers.fact: The longest visible wavelength, and the outer band of the arc.

answers.name: Blue
answers.fact: Newton placed it between green and indigo in his seven.

answers.name: Green
answers.fact: The middle band, and the wavelength the human eye is most sensitive to.

answers.name: Yellow
answers.fact: Between orange and green, and the narrowest band to most eyes.

answers.name: Orange
answers.fact: Named after the fruit, not the other way round - the colour word came later.

answers.name: Violet
answers.fact: The shortest visible wavelength, and the inner band of the arc.

answers.name: Indigo
answers.fact: Newton added it to make seven, to match the notes of a musical scale. Most people cannot pick it out.

distractors.name: Pink
distractors.note: Not a spectral colour at all - it has no single wavelength.

distractors.name: Cyan
distractors.note: A real colour, but not one of Newton's seven.

distractors.name: White
distractors.note: All wavelengths together, which is what the prism splits.
